SUBJECT : Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing
TIT
LE : Title 24 California Energy Code Certificate of Installation, Verification, and
Acceptance Compliance Requirements and San Francisco Green Building
Code Compliance Verification Requirements
PURPOSE : The purpose of this information sheet is to clarify the process for preparing and
submitting the required documentation for compliance with the Title 24 California
Energy Code and the San Francisco Green Building Code.
REFERENCE : California Energy Code (CEC), Current Edition
California Green Building Standards Code (CALGreen), Current Edition
San Francisco Green Building Code (SFGBC), Current Edition
Adm inistrative Bulletin AB-093 Implementation of Green Building Regulations
Information Sheets G-01, M-03, M-04 and M-08
DISCUSSION : Do cumentation showing compliance with the CEC and SFGBC is required to be
prepared by the responsible party and submitted to the Department of Building
Inspection (DBI). This information sheet clarifies the appropriate inspection checklists
and forms for demonstrating compliance with the i nstallation, verification and
acceptance requirements of the CEC and compliance with the SFGBC.
1. Required Title-24 CEC and SFGBC Inspections: Prior to permit approval, the applicable Title-
24 CEC and SFGBC inspection requirements shall be specified by the responsible designer using
the appropriate inspection checklists . The inspection checklists specifying the required
inspections shall be completed and affixed to the drawings submitted with the permit application.
The appropriate checklists are dependent on the project type and are contained in Information
Sheets M-03, M-04 and M-08 as follows:
• See Information Sheet M-03 for single-family residential buildings.
• See Information Sheet M -04 for non -residential, high- rise residential and hotel/motel
buildings.
• See Information Sheet M-08 for low-rise multi-family residential buildings.

The c ertificate of i nstallation documentation (checklists contained in M -03, M -04 and/or M-08) is not
required for alterations to existing residential buildings where Energy Code Compliance (ECC) field
verification is not required, such as water heater and window replacements, or additions to existing
residential buildings that are less than 300 square feet.
Each inspection item has a corresponding form code, which will be entered into DBI’s Permit Tracking
System database. Inspection items included on the checklists will be tracked for clearance prior to final
inspection and issuance of a Certificate of Final Completion and Occupancy.
2. Required Title 24 CEC and SFGBC Compliance Documentation : Documentation of
compliance with Title-24 CEC and SFGBC are required prior to a final inspection.
A. Title 24 CEC Compliance: To document compliance with Title 24 CEC requirements,
complete the appropriate Certificates of Installation, Acceptance and Verification forms
and submit a final compliance affidavit.
Title 24 CEC Certificates: Prior to final inspection of the building permit , the responsible
designer, installer and/or energy consultant shall complete the appropriate Certificates of
Installation, Acceptance and Verification forms. The specific Certificates of Installation,
Acceptance and Verification forms that are required for the project are indicated on the
applicable Title 24 CEC inspection requirements checklists prepared by the r esponsible
designer as described under Section 1 of this information sheet.
The Certificate of Installation, Acceptance and Verification forms can be found on the
California Energy Commission website at energy.ca.gov/programs-and-
topics/programs/building-energy-efficiency-standards/2025-building-energy-efficiency.
Inquiries regarding the certificates may be made by contacting the California Energy
Commission’s Energy Standard hotline at (800) 772- 3300 or emailing
title24@energy.ca.gov.
The completed and signed Certificates of Installation, Acceptance and Verification forms
shall be maintained by the building owner and shall be made available to DBI for review
upon request.
Examples of energy consultants include:
• Certified Energy Plans Examiner (CEPE): as issued by the California Association of
Building Energy Consultants (CABEC) cabec.org
• Certified Energy Analyst (CEA): as issued by the California Association of Building Energy
Consultants (CABEC) cabec.org
• Energy Code Compliance (ECC): as issued by CHEERS cheers.org
• Acceptance Test Technician (ATT) certified by a California Energy Commission
Acceptance Test Technician Certification Provider (ATTCHP)
a. Title 24 CEC Final Compliance Affidavit: After all forms required in Section 2.A above
are prepared, the responsible designer or e nergy consultant shall prepare a final

compliance affidavit certifying that all the Title 24 CEC inspection items required by
the inspection checklists described in Section 1 of this information sheet have been
completed and all documentation of installation, acceptance and verification described
in Section 2.A is complete.
The responsible designer or energy consultant shall email the final compliance affidavit to the
DBI Energy Inspection staff at dbi.energyinspections@sfgov.org. For ECC items, the affidavit
must be submitted by a certified ECC Rater. For NRCA-MCH and NRCA-LTI/LTO acceptance
tests, the affidavit must be submitted by a certified ATT for mechanical systems /lighting
controls.
Once the final compliance affidavit is received by DBI staff, the form codes corresponding to
each inspection requirement will be checked against those listed in DBI’s Permit Tracking
System database. The Certificate of Final Completion and Occupancy will not be issued until
all required Title 24 CEC inspection items are cleared.
It is the responsibility of the contractors, acceptance testers and/or ECC raters to provide all
the appropriate completed and signed certificates to the responsible designer or energy
consultant for the preparation of the final compliance affidavit . A sample affidavit is included
in Attachment 1 of this information sheet.
For R3 Occupancies, an owner/builder may submit the final compliance affidavit provided the
building permit was obtained by the owner.
The final compliance affidavit shall include the following:
b. Company l etterhead with the address and contact information of the responsible
designer or energy consultant.
c. DBI may accept the final compliance a ffidavit from a mechanical , electrical, or
plumbing contractor on mechanical, electrical, or plumbing work, respectively.
d. Project Data: project address, scope of work, building permit application number and,
if applicable, mechanical, electrical, or plumbing permit numbers.
e. A list of the required certificates as per the Title 24 CEC inspection checklists. This
shall include the form code at the end of each item specified ( i.e. NRCI -LTI-01-E
Certification of Installation- Indoor Lighting (IE6), NRCA -LTI-02 Lighting Controls
(AE1), etc.)
f. A statement indicating that all required certificates have been completed and signed.
g. First and last name, signature and contact information for the responsible party
preparing the compliance affidavit. Indicate the type of credential in the letter:
Engineer, Architect, Contractor, Owner/Builder (for Group R3 occupancy only), Energy
Consultant, Certified Acceptance Test Technician, or other responsible parties as
allowed under Information Sheet G-01.
h. State License number for engineers, architects or contractors and Certificate number
for testers, consultants and ECC testers shall be included in the letter.
i. Submittal Instructions for the Title 24 CEC Inspections Final Compliance Affidavit:
j. Email the final compliance affidavit to dbi.energyinspections@sfgov.org. Do not attach
the Title 24 Certificates or Checklists.

k. Allow 10 business days for review. Do not resubmit until 10 business days have
passed.
l. If the project is not cleared after 10 business days, do not resubmit your affidavit. Call
628-652-3407 and leave a voicemail explaining the reason for your call and providing
your permit application number and date of the final compliance affidavit. A
representative of the Special Inspections team will return your call within 72 hours.
m. After 10 business days, check the status of your affidavit online at sfgov.org/dbi. A
date under the “Completed Date” column indicates that the affidavit has been reviewed
and approved. A date in the “Completed Date” column with initials of the inspector in
the “Inspected By” column should also appear.
n. SFGBC Compliance: Compliance with the SFGBC is demonstrated in accordance with
SFGBC Administrative Bulletin AB -093, Implementation of Green Building
Regulations. To document compliance with SFGBC requirements, complete the form
contained in Attachment E of Administrative Bulletin AB -093. This requirement is
applicable to new construction and major alterations only.
o. Attachment E of Administrative Bulletin AB -093 must be completed by the Design
Professional of Record (Option 1) or the Green Building Compliance Professional of
Record (Option 2), prior to final inspection of the building permit. The completed form
shall be submitted by email along with the Title- 24 CEC Final Compliance Affidavit.
See instructions above for the submittal of the final compliance affidavit.
p. Administrative Bulletin AB-093 can be found on the SFDBI website at the following link
and is included as IS M -06 Attachment 4 as a sample:
codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/san_francisco/latest/sf_building/0-0-0-
Effective date of the provisions of this information sheet:
The 2025 Title-24 CEC inspection checklists are effective for building permit applications submitted on
or after January 1, 2026. The form contained in Attachment E of the Administrative Bulletin AB- 093 for
compliance with 2025 SFGBC is required for new construction and major alteration permits that will have
a final certificate of completion and occupancy after January 1, 2026 . For compliance with AB-093, the
2025 SFGBC and 2025 CEC inspection checklists may be used for all previous code cycles.
